comment.text: Clock attached to the back of the building showing the brand name of paper manufactured at the mill.

The Cottage as it was known within the John Dickinson Stationery Company is the original building taken on by  the company's founder in 1807 when he moved to Apsley. Attracted by the 'promise' of the Fourdrinier paper machine then being demonstrated at the neighbouring Frogmore Mill, Mr Dickinson began his own manufacturing business on the site, where in 1809 he introduced his own, 'superior', 'Cylinder Mould' paper machine.

John Dickinson was an excellent entrepreneur and his Stationery Company introduced to the world much of what we know today as stationery - postage stamps, the envelope, writing pads and accounting books to name just a few.

Dickinson's grew to operate 6 manufacturing plants in the UK, branch offices in 12 UK cities and subsidiaries in 13 countries worldwide.  Their famous brands include Lion, Three Candlesticks, Challenge, Black & Red and Basildon Bond.

The cottage and its war memorial is now owned and maintained by the Apsley Paper Trail conservation charity.
